heuristic.applicability: Prefer when scene displacement is modest or target_pose is available only as an input landmark, but TCP pose, finger state or drawer progress differs from the nominal handoff/intermediate trajectory. It is especially suitable for early-overlap switching between descending/releasing and settled/retreating states, or replanning from a partly executed approach/closure while geometry remains reachable. It still trains every action 900:1330 and the full 900:1160 overlap.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer is open or partly closed, causal TCP/q/finger/drawer observations are finite, and either release completion or later phase can be inferred from physical state; early valid entry remains constrained to block over/inside the cavity.
handoff.exit_conditions: Drawer below 0.025 and nearly stationary, object remains inside, gripper open, TCP high and clear.
handoff.failure_signatures: Local corrections drift away from handle, phase cues conflict, object remains coupled as closure starts, fingers miss handle, drawer stops above threshold, or IK is infeasible.
handoff.overlap_role: Actions 900:1160 in all demonstrations directly supervise local corrections through release completion, retreat/reorientation, handle approach and acquisition, giving action-supervised tolerance to predecessor switch timing.
handoff.successor_readiness: Terminal readiness requires observed closure and retreat, not a predicted phase or gripper sign.

heuristic.limitations: A local correction does not by itself encode a globally fixed handle or closed destination, so repeated errors, a large drawer displacement, or an unseen phase may accumulate drift. Fresh composition can preserve an existing global offset if the network emits only nominal local motion. The moving-drawer-frame prior covers large drawer displacement; the fixed closed-destination prior covers partly closed/stopping ambiguity. No contact truth is observed, and successful labels do not establish recovery from a missed grasp, jam or block interference. Rotation-vector support can also be difficult near pi, though demonstrated local increments are small.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Keep the standard DiffusionBackbone unchanged. Action dimension is 7: current-TCP-frame position delta, current-TCP-frame rotation vector, and gripper. FK of each native command supplies the target; each label is relative to its own action_observation TCP, while each decode composes with the fresh current tcp_pose before shared IK. The chunk does not update hidden phase state during denoising. Inputs retain absolute qpos/qvel plus causal relational progress features so local invariance does not discard robot configuration or articulated contact dependencies. HL should prefer this model for execution-state mismatch rather than large fixture displacement.
heuristic.rationale: Most likely failure targeted: the predecessor switches at a different release/retreat state, or execution begins between nominal phases, so an absolute trajectory aliases release, handle approach, closure and final retreat. Demonstrations show materially different index-900 states: demo12100 still has the object at z 0.124 and fingers around 0.018 each, demo12102 has z 0.079 and fingers around 0.032, and demo12104 is already settled at z 0.063 with nearly open fingers. Yet all later converge to a low handle pose around z 0.129, close from about 0.300 to 0.0022, and retreat. Learn each action as the SE(3) correction from that slot's measured TCP to its commanded TCP: local translation 3 m, local rotation vector 3 rad, gripper 1. Decode each executed slot relative to the fresh measured TCP, providing a feedback-like local correction when the realized intermediate TCP differs from the nominal future. Two-frame inputs explicitly expose drawer progress/velocity, finger width/change, TCP and object relative to target_pose, TCP-object separation, and qpos/qvel. These causal phase cues distinguish release, high clearance, handle acquisition, closure and final retreat without future observations or hidden phase memory.
heuristic.statement: TCP-local residual motion with causal phase features for variable handoff and intermediate execution states

assignment.subgoal: Ensure the block is released inside the open drawer, retreat from the cavity, approach and grasp the drawer handle, push the drawer from about 0.30 m travel to below the 0.025 closed threshold, release the handle, and retreat to a clear final pose. The intended contact target after release is the drawer handle; at early overlap states the block may still be the object being lowered/released and must not be confused with the handle. Approximate exit: drawer_position about 0.0022, block enclosed at z=0.063, open fingers, TCP high and clear.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Encode/decode reconstructs the demonstrated commanded world TCP from the corresponding measured TCP and compares FK position, rotation and unchanged gripper scalar. Unconverged IK is returned with explicit residual diagnostics.

contract.cut_relation: Uses every assigned action in [900,1330) for all 12 demonstrations and preserves all 260 supervised actions in [900,1160) overlap; it changes only causal features and Cartesian target coordinates.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [current-TCP-frame xyz correction in metres, current-TCP-frame rotation vector in radians, native gripper scalar]. Labels use that slot's measured pre-action tcp_pose and commanded TCP from native-command FK. Decode composes the correction with the freshly observed current tcp_pose and calls panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh qpos. Gripper >=0 opens and <0 closes. Slots represent t-1 through t+14; slots 1 through 8 execute.
contract.parameter_semantics: No high-level arguments. Phase and progress are inferred only from two causal physical observations. Every represented motion is relative to the measured TCP pose for its slot; decode uses the fresh current TCP pose.
